answer: Each agent weaves a cryptographic thread of signed attestations linking every new identity to a long‑lived vault of past behavior, like a meadow of footprints that only the original walker can extend. When a node proposes a transaction, peers verify the continuous chain back to the vault; any break forces the proposal to be rejected. An attacker must recreate the entire thread for each fake identity, paying proportional computational and staking costs that grow with age, making a Sybil surge economically infeasible.
